simple.meaning: עָבַשׁ (ʻâbash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to dry up.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Joel, beginning at Joel 1:17. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָבַשׁ (H5685) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָבַשׁ (ʻâbash) / H5685 is traced through Joel 1:17 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5685. abash [ עָבַשׁ ] verb shrivel (compare Arabic contract (especially face), frown ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine plural פְרֻדוֺת עָֽבְשׁוּ Joel 1:17 the grains have shrivelled (compare Dr Now).

occurrences.englishText: The seeds rot under their clods.
